A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CVE-Bench and are readable, including their figures, tables and complete appendices. The same benchmark, experiments and retained appendix content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of Cy-Agent, T-Agent and AutoGPT, including exploitation success, costs, exploit composition and case studies.

after.justification: V4 retains these empirical results and adds quantified failure modes and evaluations of standalone ZAP and T-Agent with Llama 3.1.

M1.justification: The proposed sandbox, eight attack goals and grading procedure remain unchanged. T-Agent's sqlmap adaptation and Cy-Agent's prompt adaptation already appear in v1. The added architecture and integration documentation does not establish a changed benchmark method.

E1.justification: V1 Table 5 and v4 Table 6 contain identical entries for all 40 CVEs. Application coverage, attack goals and zero-day/one-day scenarios are retained. The additional baselines and ZAP example use existing benchmark tasks.

E2.justification: Appendix D adds standalone ZAP 2.16.1 and T-Agent with Llama 3.1 alongside the original three GPT-4o agent comparisons. This substantially broadens comparison to a conventional security scanner and an open-source model. V1 mentions a ZAP team but reports no standalone ZAP evaluation.

E3.justification: The original GPT-4o version, 30-iteration budget and zero-day/one-day evaluation remain unchanged. Added evaluations introduce manually running ZAP with all options enabled and substituting Llama 3.1 in T-Agent. The new failure analysis uses independent annotation by two authors with disagreement reconciliation.

E4.justification: V1 provides qualitative failure categories and three exploitation case studies. V4 retains them but adds systematic annotation and failure frequencies across all three agents and both settings in Table 5. Figure 5 also adds a ZAP failure example, substantially strengthening the analysis of unsuccessful attacks.

E5.justification: The original five-repetition practice is unchanged and also applies to the new Llama 3.1 evaluation. Appendix D additionally specifies one execution per CVE for ZAP, justified as deterministic. Neither version provides confidence intervals, seed information or significance tests.

E6.justification: V4 corrects the zero-day/one-day maxima in Section 4.2 from 13%/25% to 10%/12.5%, matching the unchanged Figure 3 bars; this is not a measured performance decline. It also adds failure frequencies, zero successful CVEs for both additional baselines, and the ZAP example's 19 noncritical alerts. Original cost values and exploit-composition plots remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs. V4 introduces no substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions or derivations; the operational attack goals and CVSS basis remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution and abstract's approximately 13% exploitation claim remain intact. The conclusion narrows the stated zero-day/one-day maxima from 13%/25% to 10%/13%, correcting their inconsistency with the existing plot rather than redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: V4 attributes T-Agent's SQL success more specifically to coordinated tool use rather than tool availability. It identifies exploration as the dominant bottleneck, interprets differences between failure modes and discusses the GPT-4o/Llama capability gap. The stated benchmark limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices A-C substantially expand documentation: screening 60 candidates down to 40 CVEs, independent review, exclusion criteria, container organization, initialization, grader responses, prebuilt images and Inspect AI usage. V4 also clarifies shared tool access and explicitly states that reference exploits are private. These are disclosures, not evidence that the original experiments changed.

R1.justification: V4 adds discussion and citations for NYU CTF Bench, CyberSecEval 2/3, InjecAgent and Agent Security Bench, distinguishing security of AI systems from this work's focus. The central positioning against Cybench and Fang et al. remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact, with localized grammar, terminology and paragraph revisions. The appendices are reorganized: task examples and agent configurations are combined under Appendix C, while construction, architecture and additional baselines receive clearer organization.

P2.justification: V4 adds the failure-frequency table and ZAP screenshot, relocates Figure 3 and labels its axis ticks as percentages. Table captions move above tables, and the retained CVE inventory receives alternating row shading and a full-page layout. Existing plots are otherwise substantially preserved.

improvement.justification: V4 improves accuracy by aligning success-rate summaries with Figure 3, improves reproducibility documentation in Appendices A-B, and supports failure analysis with annotated frequencies. These are useful gains without changing the core benchmark. Their strength is limited by the underspecified Llama 3.1 configuration and an overgeneralized interpretation of Table 5: increased one-day tool misuse occurs for AutoGPT, not all agents.
